negative_findings.description: No supplier-registration, procurement-policy or tender page could be located for AT Universal Bank / monobank despite Ukrainian-language querying combining the bank name with закупівлі, тендер and постачальники.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches returned only product, partnership-project and Wikipedia material. The only procurement-adjacent hit was a Prozorro.sale document where the bank appears as a financial service provider, not as a buyer.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Universal Bank/monobank is one of the fastest-growing IT-intensive banks in Ukraine and a plausible large buyer of payment and technology hardware/services. Its vendor spend is currently entirely opaque, leaving a real hole in the non-state demand picture.

negative_findings.description: No procurement or supplier-onboarding section was located for A-Bank (abank.ua).
negative_findings.result_summary: Ukrainian-language queries on the bank name plus тендер/закупівлі/постачальникам returned only unrelated Prozorro records where banks appear as service providers, and pages belonging to other institutions (PrivatBank, Ukrgasbank, UkrSibbank, NBU).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A-Bank is a sizeable retail/card issuer in the cell. Absence of any published vendor channel means it can only ever be reached through the commercial marketplaces or direct outreach, which should be reflected in coverage expectations.

negative_findings.description: PUMB (First Ukrainian International Bank) has no discoverable procurement or supplier-registration page on its own web properties.
negative_findings.result_summary: Ukrainian-language queries surfaced only PUMB's client-facing business banking, factoring-for-Prozorro-suppliers products, and document templates. The only buy-side visibility found was PUMB's issuer page on the Zakupivli.Pro commercial marketplace (EDRPOU 14282829).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: PUMB is the largest Ukrainian-capital private bank in the cell; the fact that its only public procurement window is a third-party marketplace confirms the cell's core hypothesis and makes marketplace coverage non-optional rather than supplementary.

negative_findings.description: ProCredit Bank Ukraine's tender page presents itself as a tender listing but its most recent entries date from 2008.
negative_findings.result_summary: Fetched page shows completed tenders for 2008-2009 (vehicle insurance, website development, office-equipment vendors) and no active procurements; the live element is a cooperation-proposal intake form.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Demonstrates that the presence of a bank tender page is not evidence of an active feed. Any verification pass should distinguish 'page live' from 'content current', or the source inventory will overstate real coverage.

negative_findings.description: BNP Paribas Group states it does not practise open bidding, which structurally caps what UkrSibbank can ever publish.
negative_findings.result_summary: Group supplier page: suppliers are either added to a preferred-supplier list following a call for tenders or picked for a specific project, with pre-qualification on financial soundness and economic dependence; contracting runs through the group OneProcTool/Ivalua platform.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms that the absence of a UkrSibbank tender board is deliberate policy, not a discovery failure. Collection effort for this bank should be redirected from tender-watching to onboarding-channel and group-policy monitoring.

negative_findings.description: Raiffeisen Bank Ukraine's actual tender workflow runs on Oracle iProcurement and a Microsoft Forms supplier questionnaire, neither of which exposes a public listing.
negative_findings.result_summary: The public procurement page names the tooling and the intake form but publishes no tender announcements; announcements appear instead on E-Tender and Zakupivli.Pro.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The authoritative system of record is closed. Collection must rely on the marketplace mirrors, which may carry only a subset of the bank's procurements — coverage from these feeds should be treated as partial by construction.

negative_findings.description: The Ukrainian/Russian term 'тендер' plus a bank name is heavily polluted by sell-side and unrelated results.
negative_findings.result_summary: Queries repeatedly returned tender-guarantee products (тендерна гарантія) that banks sell to bidders, Prozorro records where the bank is the winning provider of banking services, and Russian-market Raiffeisenbank RU results (rostender.info, zakupki.kontur.ru) that must be excluded.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Without disambiguation a collector will conflate a bank selling tender guarantees with a bank buying goods, and will pull Russian-jurisdiction data into a Ukraine run. Noisy terms must be flagged and the Russian domains blocklisted.

negative_findings.description: No general procurement or vendor page was located for Bank Pivdenny; only a statutory audit-firm selection competition was observed.
negative_findings.result_summary: Ukrainian-language search surfaced the bank's tender-guarantee product page and an audit-firm selection competition dated 14.08.2026, but no procurement section. Note the bank operates on bank.com.ua rather than the assumed pivdenny.ua.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: For this bank the only forced-disclosure lever is regulatory (mandatory audit selection). Domain assumptions in the seed brief were wrong, which is itself a caution for automated URL construction.

coverage_gaps.description: Three of the eight named cell banks — Universal/monobank, A-Bank and Pivdenny — have no working direct source; only marketplace and registry proxies exist, and for monobank and A-Bank not even that was confirmed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run EDRPOU-scoped sweeps for these three across Zakupivli.Pro, SmartTender and E-Tender to establish whether they issue commercial tenders at all; if not, downgrade them to outreach-only targets and record the finding rather than continuing to search.

coverage_gaps.description: Bank-issuer coverage on the three commercial marketplaces was established only for the banks reached by name search; there was no systematic enumeration of which financial institutions are tenants on each platform.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Register free supplier accounts on Zakupivli.Pro, SmartTender.biz and E-Tender, then enumerate issuers filtered to banking/finance to discover banks that publish nowhere else. This is likely to yield actors outside the eight-bank seed list.

coverage_gaps.description: Tender documentation — the layer holding technical specifications and qualification requirements — generally sits behind free but mandatory supplier registration on the marketplaces, and behind APS-TENDER for OTP.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Decide policy on registered-account collection, including ToS review for each platform, before building collectors. Headline-only collection will capture demand timing but not requirement detail.

coverage_gaps.description: Snowballing surfaced foreign-owned private banks outside the seed list — KredoBank (PKO BP), ProCredit Bank, Piraeus Bank MKB — that fit the cell's definition exactly.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Formally extend the cell's actor map to all foreign-parent private banks operating in Ukraine rather than the eight seeded names, and repeat the direct-page sweep across the extended list.

coverage_gaps.description: Parent-group procurement policy was searched in English only; parent-language sources (Hungarian for OTP, French for BNP Paribas and Credit Agricole, Polish for PKO BP/KredoBank) were not systematically covered.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run parent-language queries (beszállítói etikai kódex, charte achats responsables fournisseurs, kodeks dostawcy) since group procurement portals and supplier codes are frequently published first or only in the parent language.

coverage_gaps.description: Several dated policy artefacts were identified but not retrieved in this pass: Raiffeisen's standard contractual terms (04/2024, 04/2025), Credit Agricole's procurement roadmap and mandatory clauses (06/2024, 05/2020), UkrSibbank's Suppliers' CSR Charter, and KredoBank's tender-participant ethics code.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a PDF capture-and-version job for these documents; dated editions make them a clean change-detection signal for shifts in vendor requirements.

coverage_gaps.description: Russian-jurisdiction procurement sites (rostender.info, zakupki.kontur.ru) and sell-side tender-guarantee product pages contaminate every 'bank + тендер' query.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Blocklist Russian procurement domains in the run configuration and add a negative filter for тендерна гарантія / tender guarantee product pages before running automated discovery.

brief: Private and foreign-owned banks in Ukraine sit entirely outside public procurement law, and the cell splits cleanly into three tiers of visibility. A minority publish genuinely usable direct sources: OTP Bank is the outlier with both a full published tender rulebook and a live, dated tender board that sometimes names winners, while Credit Agricole and Raiffeisen publish detailed onboarding routes (questionnaire, vendor mailbox, dated standard terms) without publishing the tenders themselves. A second tier — UkrSibbank, ProCredit, PUMB — offers only a supplier expression-of-interest form or nothing at all, with UkrSibbank's opacity confirmed as deliberate BNP group policy against open bidding; for these, the three commercial marketplaces (Zakupivli.Pro, E-Tender, SmartTender.biz), queryable by buyer EDRPOU, are the only demand-side window and should be treated as the backbone of collection rather than a supplement. A third tier — monobank/Universal, A-Bank, Pivdenny — yielded no procurement channel at all in Ukrainian-language search, leaving parent-group supplier codes (RBI, BNP, OTP Group) and regulatory forced-disclosure such as audit-firm selection competitions as the residual signal.
